                        ( p. 315 ) H ترا तिरा tirā (contrac. of terā , gen. of tū ), pron. adj. Thy, thine (used chiefly in poetry). 2) تراس tirās, trās
                        ( p. 315 ) H تراس तिरास tirās , त्रास trās [S. तृषा ], s.f. Thirst ( = tis ; pyās ): — tirās ānā , tirās lagnā , v.n. To be thirsty. 3) تراسي tirāsī
                        ( p. 315 ) H تراسي तिरासी tirāsī [Prk. त्रिआसी ; S. त्र्यशीति ], adj. Eighty-three. 4) ترانا tirānā, tarānā
                        ( p. 315 ) H ترانا तिराना tirānā , तराना tarānā (caus. of tirnā or tairnā ), v.t. To cause to pass over or across, to cause the salvation (of), to save; to make (one) swim; to cause to float. 5) ترانو tirānav, tirānau
                        ( p. 315 ) H ترانو तिरानव tirānav , tirānau , adj. = next, q.v. 6) ترانوي tirānwe, tirānawwe, tirānawe
                        ( p. 315 ) H ترانوي तिरान्वे tirānwe तिरीनव्वे tirānawwe tirānawe [S. त्रिनवति ], adj. Ninety-three. 7) تراني tirānī, tarānī
                        ( p. 315 ) H تراني तिरानी tirānī , तरानी tarānī (fr. tirānā ), s.f. 'A crossing over'; a bribe given on condition that it be returned if the suit is lost. 8) تراو tirāʼo, tarāʼo
                        ( p. 315 ) H تراو तिराव tirāʼo , तराव tarāʼo [ tirā ( nā )+ āʼo = Prk. एअव्वं = S. ( इ ) तव्यं ], s.m. Crossing over; swimming. 9) تراونا tirāwnā, tirāʼonā
                        ( p. 315 ) H تراونا तिरावना tirāwnā , or tirāʼonā , v.t. = tirānā , q.v. 10) ترائي tirāʼī, tarāʼī
                        ( p. 316 ) H ترائي तिराई tirāʼī , तराई tarāʼī [ tirā ( nā )+ āʼī = Prk. एअव्व अइआ = S. aff. ( इ ) तव्य + ता + इका ], s.f. = tirānī , q.v. 11) ترباچك tir-bāćak
                        ( p. 316 ) H ترباچك तिर्बाचक tir-bāćak [S. त्रि + वाचक ], s.m. An agreement confirmed three times. 12) تربد tirbid, turbad, turbud
                        ( p. 316 ) P تربد tirbid , turbad , turbud (S. त्रिवृत् ), s.m. A plant of valuable cathartic properties, a purgative Indian root, turpeth, Convolvulus (and Ipomæa ) turpethum (syn. teʼoṛī ). 13) تربهر tirbhir
                        ( p. 316 ) H تربهر तिरभिर tirbhir [S. तिमिर ], adj. 'Blinded with rage,' enraged (cf. tirmirā ; and tirī-birī ). 14) ترپن tirpan
                        ( p. 316 ) H ترپن तिरपन tirpan [Prk. त्रिपण्मं ; S. त्रिपञ्चाशत् ], adj. Fifty-three: — tirpan-bel , s.f. A kind of embroidery in the form or a creeper with flowers. 15) ترتا tirtā
                        ( p. 316 ) H ترتا तिरता tirtā [S. त्रितयं ?], adj. Treble, triple, three-fold. 16) ترترانا tirtirānā
                        ( p. 317 ) H ترترانا तिरतिराना tirtirānā [S. त्ऋ redupl., or perhaps another form of tartarānā ], v.n. To drop, to trickle. 17) ترچها tirćhā
                        ( p. 317 ) H ترچها तिर्छा , तिरछा tirćhā [Prk. तिरिच्छओ ; S. तिर्यच् + क + कः ], adj. (f. - ī ), Across, athwart, planting, oblique, crosswise, crooked, bent, awry, askant; perverse; foolish; affected, foppish: — tirćhā dekhnā , v.n. To look askant, to squint: — tirćhā karnā , v.t. To place across, place transversely or obliquely; to slant, to incline: — tirćhā lagnā (- meṅ ), To strike obliquely, to glance: — tirćhī āṅkh karnā (- par ) = tirćhī nigāh-se dekhnā (- ko ), To look askance (at); to look angrily (at): — tirćhī naz̤ar , s.f. Side glance; leer, ogle; squint. 18) ترچهانا tirćhānā
                        ( p. 317 ) H ترچهانا तिरछाना tirćhānā [ tirćhā , q.v.+ ā = āw = Prk. आव or आवे = S. आपआ (caus. augment.)+ nā = Prk. अणअं = S. अनीयं ], v.t. To place in a transverse position, &c. ( = tirćhā karnā , q.v.); — v.n. To be perverse; to be affected, be foppish. 19) ترچهيانا tirćhiyānā
                        ( p. 317 ) H ترچهيانا तिरछियाना tirćhiyānā , (i.q. tirćhānā , with tirchī , instead of tirćhā ), v.n. To edge, to go obliquely. 20) ترس tiras
                        ( p. 318 ) S ترس तिरस tiras , adv. Crookedly, obliquely, awry; transversely; indirectly, secretly, covertly (a particle of abuse or depreciation): — tiras-kār s.m. tiṛas-kriyā , s.f. Disrespect, abuse, reproach, censure' disgrace; disdain, contempt; — tiras-kār karnā , v.t. To' disgrace, dishonour; to abuse, revile, &c.: — tiras-kr̤ita , part. Censured, reviled, abused, reproached; scorned: — tiras-karī , s.f. A curtain, veil, screen of cloth drawn across a tent or apartment. 21) ترسٿ tirsaṭ
                        ( p. 318 ) H ترسٿ तिरसट tirsaṭ , adj. = next, q.v. 22) ترسٿهہ tirsaṭh
                        ( p. 318 ) H ترسٿهہ तिरसठ tirsaṭh [Prk. त्रिसट्ठी ; S. त्रिषष्टिः ], adj. Sixty-three ( = trěsaṭh ). 23) ترسکار tiras-kār
                        ( p. 318 ) S ترسکار तिरस्कार tiras-kār , s.m. See s.v. tiras for compounds. 24) ترکها tirkhā
                        ( p. 319 ) H ترکها तिरखा tirkhā , s.f. = tr̤ishā , q.v. 25) ترکهت tirkhit
                        ( p. 319 ) H ترکهت तिरखित tirkhit , part. adj. = tr̤ishit , q.v. 26) ترکهنٿي tirkhuṅṭī
                        ( p. 319 ) H ترکهنٿي तिरखुंटी tirkhuṅṭī , = H ترکهونٿ तिरखूंट tirkhūṅṭ , = H ترکهونٿي तिरखूंटी tirkhūṅṭī , [S. त्रि + कूटं , or खण्डं + इका ], s.f. A three-sided figure, triangle; trivet, tripod; a kind of triangular weapon; a triangular cake of salt: — tirkhūṅṭ-sā , adj. (Bot.), Deltoid, delta-leaved. 27) ترکهونٿ tirkhūṅṭ
                        ( p. 319 ) H ترکهونٿ तिरखूंट tirkhūṅṭ , = H ترکهنٿي तिरखुंटी tirkhuṅṭī , = H ترکهونٿي तिरखूंटी tirkhūṅṭī , [S. त्रि + कूटं , or खण्डं + इका ], s.f. A three-sided figure, triangle; trivet, tripod; a kind of triangular weapon; a triangular cake of salt: — tirkhūṅṭ-sā , adj. (Bot.), Deltoid, delta-leaved. 28) ترکهونٿي tirkhūṅṭī
                        ( p. 319 ) H ترکهونٿي तिरखूंटी tirkhūṅṭī , = H ترکهنٿي तिरखुंटी tirkhuṅṭī , = H ترکهونٿ तिरखूंट tirkhūṅṭ , [S. त्रि + कूटं , or खण्डं + इका ], s.f. A three-sided figure, triangle; trivet, tripod; a kind of triangular weapon; a triangular cake of salt: — tirkhūṅṭ-sā , adj. (Bot.), Deltoid, delta-leaved. 29) ترمرا tirmirā
                        ( p. 320 ) H ترمرا तिर्मिरा tirmirā [S. तिमिर + कं ], s.m. 'Darkness in the eyes,' sensation of being dazzled; an ocular spectrum or spark appearing before the eye (from the internal state of that organ; cf. tirmirī ); a spot of oil or grease swimming on water or any other liquid. 30) ترمراتا tirmirātā
                        ( p. 320 ) H ترمراتا तिर्मिराता tirmirātā (imperf. part. of next), adj. (f. - ī ), Dazzling, &c. 31) ترمراتا tirmirānā
                        ( p. 320 ) H ترمراتا तिर्मिराना tirmirānā [ tirmirā + ā = āw = Prk. आव = S. आपि (caus. augment)+ nā = Prk. अणअं = S. अनीयं ], v.n. To dazzle; to be dazed; to be dizzy; to quiver, vibrate, thrill, shake; to glisten as oil or grease swimming on water, &c. 32) ترمراهٿ tirmirāhaṭ
                        ( p. 320 ) H ترمراهٿ तिर्मिराहट tirmirāhaṭ [ tirmirā ( nā )+ āhat = āwaṭ = Prk. एअव्वअ + ट्टं = S. ( इ ) तव्य + क + त्वं ], s.f. Dazzling; glistening; quivering, vibration; becoming dizzy. 33) ترمري tirmirī
                        ( p. 320 ) H ترمري तिर्मिरी tirmirī [S. तिमिर + इका ], s.f. Darkness before the eyes, dizziness, swimming in the head, giddiness, vertigo ( = tewar ). 34) ترنا tirnā
                        ( p. 320 ) H ترنا तिरना tirnā (see tīrnā or tairnā ), v.n. To swim; to float; to go over or across, &c. ( = tarnā ): — tir-jānā , v.n. (intensive) To go across, swim across: — tirtā phirnā , v.n. To be swimming or floating about, to swim about. 35) ترودشي tirodaśī
                        ( p. 321 ) H ترودشي तिरोदशी tirodaśī , s.f. = trayo-daśī , q.v. 36) تروندا tirauṅdā
                        ( p. 321 ) H تروندا तिरौंदा tirauṅdā [S. तरण्ड + कः with व inserted], s.m. A float; a buoy; a beacon. 37) تروهت tiro-hit
                        ( p. 321 ) S تروهت तिरोहित tiro-hit , part. Covered, concealed, hidden, removed or withdrawn from sight. 38) ترهت tirhut
                        ( p. 321 ) H ترهت तिरहुत tirhut [S. तीरभुक्तिः ], s.f. The district of Tirhut in Bengal. 39) ترهتيا tirhutigā
                        ( p. 321 ) H ترهتيا तिर्हुतिया tirhutigā [ tirhut +S. ईय + कः ], adj. & s.m. Of or belonging to Tirhut; produced or made in Tirhut; — a native of Tirhut. 40) ترياق tiryāq
                        ( p. 321 ) A ترياق tiryāq (supposed to be the Gr. θηριακὰ Arabicized), s.m. Theriac (also called 'treacle'), an antidote (for poisons, snake-bites, &c.); Bezoar stone; a sovereign remedy; opium (because it is a remedy for anxiety, &c.): — tiryāq-ě-fāruq , tiryāq-fāruq , s.m. The best kind of tiryāq . 41) ترياقي tiryāqī
                        ( p. 321 ) A ترياقي tiryāqī , adj. & s.m. Intoxicated; — an opium-eater. 42) ترياك tiryāk
                        ( p. 321 ) P ترياك tiryāk , s.m. = tiryāq , q.v. 43) تري بري tirī-birī
                        ( p. 321 ) H تري بري तिरीबिरी tirī-birī , adj. Dispersed, scattered ( = titar-bitar ). 44) تريك tiryak
                        ( p. 322 ) S تريك तिर्यक् tiryak (from tiryać ), adv. Across, obliquely, transversely, horizontally (occurring in comp., when the final k is liable to be changed to g ): — tiryag , tiryag-ga , adj. & s.m. Going obliquely, going across or horizontally; — an animal: — tiryag-ja , adj. Born from an animal, brute-born: — tiryag-yona , s.m. An animal; brute, quadruped: — tiryag-yoni , s.f. The womb of an animal; the animal creation, organic nature. 45) تريکتا tiryaktā
                        ( p. 322 ) S تريکتا तिर्यक्ता tiryaktā , s.f. The state of going across or obliquely; the state of a beast or animal, animal nature. 46) ترينچ tiryaṅć
                        ( p. 322 ) S ترينچ तिर्यंच् tiryaṅć , adv. = tiryak , q.v.; — s.m. An animal; a brute; an amphibious animal. 47) تريند tireṅd
                        ( p. 322 ) H تريند तिरेंद tireṅd , = H تريندا तिरेंदा tireṅdā , [S. तरण्डं , or तरित्र + कं ], s.m. The float of a fishing line; a float; a buoy ( = taret ). 48) تريندا tireṅdā
                        ( p. 322 ) H تريندا तिरेंदा tireṅdā , = H تريند तिरेंद tireṅd , [S. तरण्डं , or तरित्र + कं ], s.m. The float of a fishing line; a float; a buoy ( = taret ). 49) تڙهمنہا tiṛh-muṅhā
                        ( p. 323 ) H تڙهمنہا तिढ़मुंहा tiṛh-muṅhā [S. तिर्यक् + मुख + कः ; see ṭeṛhā ], adj. Wry-mouthed. 50) تير tīr
                        ( p. 351 ) S تير तीर tīr , s.m. Shore, bank; margin, brink, edge; — postpn. & adv. Near (to, - ke ), close at hand: — tīra-bhukti , s.m. The province of Tirhut, lying to the north of Bihār: — tīra-ja , tīraj , adj. & s.m. Growing or standing near a shore; — a tree near a shore. 51) تير tīr
                        ( p. 351 ) P تير tīr [S. तृतीया ], s.f. The fourth solar month of the Persian year (corresponding to the Hindī Sāwan ); the festival held on the third day of the lunar fortnight of the month Sāwan ( = tīj ): — tīr-teʼohār , s.m. = tīj-teʼohār , q.v. 52) تير tīr
                        ( p. 351 ) P تير tīr [Old P. tigra ; Zend tighri , rt. tij = S. तिज् ; S. तीर , prob. fr. P.], s.m. An arrow; — a beam, a mast; — the planet Mercury ( = tīr-ě-falak ): — tīr-andāz , s.m. An archer, a bowman: — tīr-andāzī , s.f. Archery: — tīr-bārān , s.m. A shower of arrows; a punishment in which the culprit is shot with arrows: — tīr-ba-hadaf , adj. lit . 'An arrow to the mark'; hitting the mark; to the point: — tīr-bhāl , adj. ( Bot .), Sagittate: — tīr-partāb , s.m. The range of an arrow, bow-shot distance: — tīr-pheṅknā , tīr ćalānā , tīr ćhoṛnā , v.n. To shoot an arrow; ( iron. ) to do something wonderful, to do great things: — tīr-ě-ḵẖākī , tīr-ḵẖākī , s.f. A light, small-headed arrow: — tīr-ḵẖẉurda , adj. & s.m. Struck or wounded by an arrow; — one so struck, &c.: — tīr-ras , s.m. The range of an arrow, bowshot distance: — tīr-zan , s.m. An archer: — tīr-sā , adj. & adv. Dart-like; as by an arrow: — tīr-ě-falak , s.m. The planet Mercury: — tīr-kārī , s.f. The piercing of the body by an arrow: — tīr-kā-fāṣila , s.m. The range of an arrow, &c. ( = tīr-ras , q.v.): — tīr karnā or kar-denā , v.t. To put out of sight; to hide; to make away with: — tīr-kash , s.m. A quiver; an embrasure; an aperture, a loop-hole: — tīr-kī mār , s.f. = tīr-kā fāṣila , q.v.: — tīr-gar , s.m. A maker of arrows: — tīr-garī , s.f. Arrow-making: — tīr lagnā (- meṅ , - ko ), To be struck or hit by an arrow (a mark or other object): — tīr-mār , s.m. A viper; a viper's teeth: — tīr mārnā (- ko ), To strike (an object) with an arrow; to shoot an arrow (at an object), &c. = tīr ćalānā , q.v.: — tīr-ě-nāwak , s.m. An arrow discharged through a tube: — tīr nikālnā nathnoṅ-meṅ-se (- ke ), To torture, torment, harass, persecute: — tīroṅ-se uṛānā , v.t. To do to death with arrows: — thothe tīroṅ-se uṛanā , v.t. To put to a lingering death, to kill by degrees, to torture. 53) تيرتهہ tīrth, tīrath
                        ( p. 351 ) S تيرتهہ तीर्थ tīrth , & H. तीरथ tīrath , s.m. A bathing place, a shrine or sacred place of pilgrimage (as Benares, &c. especially particular spots along the course of sacred streams, as the Ganges, &c.); pilgrimage: — tīrath-jātrā , s.m. Pilgrimage: — tīrath-rāj , tīrth-pati , s.m. An epithet of Pryāg or Ilāhābad , the chief place of pilgrimage (though inferior in point of sanctity to Banāras , to which latter place the Hindū goes rather to die than to bathe): — tīrth-kār , s.m. A holy personage: — tīrath karnā (- kā ), To go on a pilgrimage (to). 54) تيرج tīraj
                        ( p. 351 ) H تيرج तीरज tīraj , s.f. = terīj , q.v. 55) تيرگي tīragī
                        ( p. 351 ) P تيرگي tīragī (abst. subst. from tīra , q.v.), s.f. Darkness, obscurity, gloom. 56) تيرمار tīr-mār
                        ( p. 351 ) P تيرمار tīr-mār , s.m. See s.v. tīr . 57) تيرنه tīrṇa
                        ( p. 351 ) S تيرنه तीर्ण tīrṇa (rt. तॄ ), part. Crossed, passed over; spread, expanded: — tīrṇa-padī , s.f. The plant Curculigo orchioides . 58) تيره tīra
                        ( p. 351 ) P تيره tīra [Pehl. tireh ; Zend, tāthra , rt. tam ; S. timira , rt. tam ], adj. Obscure, dark, black: — tīra-abr , s.m. Black clouds: — tīra-baḵẖt , Unfortunate: — tīra-baḵẖtī , s.f. Misfortune, adversity: — tīra-dil , adj. & s.m. Ignorant, stolid, black-hearted, malicious; — apostate, outcast: — tīra-rang , adj. Turbid, muddy-coloured; black: — tīra-rozgār , adj. Unfortunate: — tīra-rozī , s.f. Misfortune, adversity. 59) ٿريندا ṭirendā
                        ( p. 357 ) H ٿريندا टिरेन्दा ṭirendā , s.m. corr. of tirendā , q.v. 60) ٿير ṭīr
                        ( p. 367 ) H ٿير टीर ṭīr [S. तिरस् , rt. तॄ ], s.f. A transverse piece in cloths, a breadth cut diagonally. 61) ٿيڙي ṭīṛī
                        ( p. 367 ) H ٿيڙي टीड़ी ṭīṛī , s.f. A locust = ṭiḍḍī , q.v. 62) طراز t̤irāz, t̤arāz
                        ( p. 752 ) A طراز t̤irāz or t̤arāz (the Ar. form of P. تراز ), s.m. Variegated or figured work (on a garment or on cloth), embroidery; ornamentation, ornament (syn. ʻalam ); ornamental border; fringe, lace; — manner, form ( = t̤arz ); — act. part. (of P. t̤irāzīdan , fr. t̤irāz ), Ornamenting with needlework; adorning, &c. (used as last member of compounds, e.g. dībāja-t̤irāz , 'composer of prefaces or exordiums,' which are generally written in a highly ornamented style). 63) طرفيل t̤irfīl, t̤arfīl
                        ( p. 752 ) A طرفيل t̤irfīl , or t̤arfīl (?), s.m. Trefoil, clover. Search Form • DDSA Close

                        ( p. 475 ) A جذر ḥaẕar (inf. n. of حذر 'to be cautious'), s.m. Caution, wariness, vigilance, care; prudence; — fear. 2) حضر ḥaẓar
                        ( p. 478 ) A حضر ḥaẓar (v.n. fr. حضر 'to be present'), s.m. Presence, residence at home; fixed residence, home; resting, remaining in a place (opp. of safar ). 3) هذر haẕar
                        ( p. 1222 ) A هذر haẕar (inf. n. of هذر 'to be nonsensical or frivolous'), s.m. Loquacity, garrulity, frivolous talk, nonsense; raving, delirium. 4) هزار hazār
                        ( p. 1228 ) P هزار hazār [Zend hazaṅra ; S. सहस्त्र ], adj. & coll. s.m. Thousand; — a thousand; — a bird called 'the thousand voices,' the nightingale (i.q. hazār-dāstān ): — hazār-pā , s.m. A centipede, scolopendra: — hazār-ćashma , s.m. Cancer (the disease): — hazār-ḵẖāna , adj. 'Having a thousand cells'; — honey-combed; — s.m. The second stomach (of beasts), tripe: — hazār-dāstān or dastān , s.m. The nightingale ( lit. 'of a thousand tales'): — hazār rang badalnā , To vary or change greatly; to be very fickle: — hazār-gāʼīda , or hazār-meḵẖī , s.f. A common strumpet; a harridan. 5) هزارا hazārā
                        ( p. 1228 ) H هزارا hazārā , s.m. = هزاره hazāra , q.v. 6) هزاران hazārān, hazārāṅ
                        ( p. 1228 ) P هزاران hazārān , vulg. hazārāṅ , s.m. pl. (of hazār ), Thousands; — a thousand; — a nightingale; — a term used in the game of nard . 7) هزاروان hazārwāṅ
                        ( p. 1228 ) H هزاروان हज़ारवां hazārwāṅ [ hazār , q.v.+Ap. Prk. अवँओ = Prk. अमओ = S. अ + म + कः ], adj. (f. - wīṅ ), Thousandth. 8) هزارون hazāroṅ
                        ( p. 1228 ) H هزارون हज़ारों hazāroṅ [ hazār + oṅ = Ap. Prk. अण्हहुं = Prk. अण्हं = S. ( आ ) नाम् suff. of gen. pl.], coll. s. pl.
